quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you start driving. This is part of getting ready to drive safely. Also adjust your seat, fasten your safety belt, and secure items in your vehicle. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: If your car has airbags, should you wear a seat belt?

options.text: Seat belts should still be worn.
Seat belts do not need to be worn.
Seat belts should be worn behind the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags and seat belts work together. Always wear your seat belt, even in cars with airbags. Use both your lap and shoulder belts for the best protection.

questions.question: The light is green, but a police officer signals you to stop. What should you do?

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic signal.
Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's signals. Follow their instructions even if they go against traffic lights, signs, or road markings.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: You are on a hill or curve.
You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.
You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross it to change lanes. A solid line means you cannot cross it. Only pass when it is safe and the road markings allow it.

questions.question: Who can use handicap parking spaces?

options.text: Only drivers with the appropriate license plate or hanging tag.
To anyone, but only if all other spaces are occupied.
To people who are not feeling well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only drivers with the appropriate license plate or hanging tag.
questions.explanation: You can only park in a handicap space if you have a special license plate or hanging tag. These spaces are reserved for people with disabilities.

questions.question: What is the only thing that reduces blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating foods high in fat
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Caffeine and food do not help.

questions.question: What should you do before turning on the ignition?

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Before you start your car, buckle your own seat belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs too.

questions.question: A person with a guide dog is crossing in front of you. You want to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses the street.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.
Wait until the person crosses the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the person crosses the street.
questions.explanation: People using guide dogs always have the right-of-way. Wait for them to cross before you turn.

questions.question: Can you drive if medication impairs your driving ability?

options.text: Under no circumstances.
If you don't feel drowsy.
If it is prescribed by a physician.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: Never drive if any medication impairs your driving. This includes prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs. Always check medication labels before driving.

questions.question: When must you obey a school crossing guard?

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Unless you do not see any children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always obey school crossing guards. Follow their instructions whenever you see them.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol from your system?

options.text: Breathe in some fresh air.
Give your body time.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give your body time.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Fresh air, coffee, and exercise do not help. You must wait.

questions.question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol from your body?

options.text: Drink strong coffee.
Wait.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee and showers do not speed this up.

questions.question: When entering a main road from a private road, what should you do?

options.text: Have the right-of-way.
Should yield to traffic already on the road.
Should honk at other drivers to get them to move more quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to traffic already on the road.
questions.explanation: When entering a main road from a private road, let traffic on the main road go first. Also yield to pedestrians on any sidewalk crossing the private road.

questions.question: Why should you give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: They do not have the same physical reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and more difficult to see than adults.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are harder to see and react slower than adults. Watch carefully for children near schools, parks, and playgrounds. They may ride bikes onto the road without warning.

questions.question: How should you enter a gap in highway traffic?

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before you change lanes, look in your mirrors and check the side of your vehicle. Make sure no cars are in the lane you want to enter.

questions.question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Drive at the posted speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Wet, snowy, or icy roads reduce tire grip. You should slow down to stay safe.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are prohibited.
You may proceed if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road. If you see it, traffic is coming toward you. Do not enter. Turn around.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving is a distraction because:

options.text: It makes you worry about the cost of the call.
It takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
It distracts other drivers around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Cell phone use while driving is dangerous because it uses your hands, eyes, and mind. Even skilled drivers increase their crash risk when using a phone.

questions.question: "No passing zone" signs tell drivers:

options.text: To speed up slightly.
That it is not safe to pass.
To maintain a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass other vehicles in that area. Poor visibility makes passing unsafe.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped ahead with red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow to no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights mean the bus is picking up or dropping off students. You must stop and wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is raised. Never pass a school bus loading or unloading.

questions.question: If you become tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop to rest or change drivers.
Drink coffee.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or change drivers.
questions.explanation: Fatigue slows your reactions and dulls your mind, making driving unsafe. Stop to rest or let someone else drive.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Stop sign ahead.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that wet pavement is slippery and dangerous. Slow down on wet roads because it takes longer to stop.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Stare directly in front of their car.
Only focus on the middle of the road.
Watch beside, ahead, and to the rear of their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch beside, ahead, and to the rear of their car.
questions.explanation: Good drivers watch all around their vehicle. Know what is happening in front, behind, and to the sides of your car.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Keep your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and be alert. Workers may be present. Follow posted speed limits.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol may affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol impair judgment and coordination. This happens even below the legal limit. Driving under the influence can result in criminal charges.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This yellow and black sign shows a pedestrian crosswalk. Watch for people crossing and let them pass safely.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to another car's rear bumper):

options.text: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
Cannot result in a traffic ticket.
Prevents being cut off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is unsafe and often leads to aggressive driving. You can receive a traffic ticket for tailgating.

questions.question: What happens if you take a prescription drug while drinking alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
You will be more alert.
You may not be fit to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not be fit to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair your driving. Mixing them with alcohol is especially dangerous.

questions.question: Before returning to your lane after passing, you should:

options.text: Beep your horn.
See both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing, only return to your lane when you can see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks. Vehicles must stop for pedestrians at marked or unmarked crossings.
